runde1.aufgabe_de: Fernunterricht: Sollten Schülerinnen und Schüler von zu Hause aus am Unterricht teilnehmen können?
runde1.text: Imagine you are attending classes at home you wouldn' t take it seriously as you do at school. Kids who are home schooled don't usually focus as much as they would at school. Some kids parents or tutor would give them more advantages that aren't given at school. Such as more breaks, better food options for lunch,linear schedule, and starting and ending time being optional. If students are learning a specific lesson by a video conference they wouldnt benefit the lesson as well as being offline. Students wouldn't benefit from being able to attend classes from home because they would take advantage, start on their own time, and they wouldn't understand the lesson.

runde1.aufgabe_de: Sommerprojekte: Sollten Lehrkräfte oder die Schülerinnen und Schüler selbst die Ferienprojekte gestalten?
runde1.text: Should these summer projects be teacher-designed or student-designed? Teachers should design the project because it will help students be stress free, give students a general idea of the project, and time management ability. Summer is to enjoy and to relax, and a teacher-designed project will allow students to do so. What student would want to stress over the summer because they can't think of a project idea? A teacher-designed project will help students be stress free because students would get a teacher-made rubric which will support them. Students are poured with stress during school, and when summer is time to relax, students should not have to worry about a project idea.

runde1.aufgabe_de: Fernunterricht: Sollten Schülerinnen und Schüler von zu Hause aus am Unterricht teilnehmen können?
runde1.text: Students that use the way of the internet to execute their online work, should have the choice to either take online classes or physically be in the classroom. In a way, online classes help the student if they obtain a focusing disability, the course can be slowed down, and the student can take their time while also having the ability to learn. Also, physically being in a class can be very distracting because of other students, video games that may be brought to class, or just the loudness a class can come up to. Online classes give a student and their teacher hands on with teaching, if there is something interrupting the students lesson mentally, teachers can figure out and pin point the main problem easier and faster than in a classroom filled with twenty or more kids.

runde1.aufgabe_de: Fernunterricht: Sollten Schülerinnen und Schüler von zu Hause aus am Unterricht teilnehmen können?
runde1.text: Everyone my age remembers the year we did school through a laptop screen. At first it sounded amazing. No alarm at six, no dress code, class in pajamas. But after a couple of months, most of us were bored, behind, and kind of lonely. That experience is why I don't think students would really benefit from being able to attend classes from home. Distance learning might sound convenient, but school is about more than just getting information, and online classes leave out a lot of what actually helps students learn and grow. My first reason is that it is way too easy to get distracted at home. When you're sitting in a classroom, the teacher can see you, and the people around you are working too, so you kind of go along with it.

runde1.aufgabe_de: Sommerprojekte: Sollten Lehrkräfte oder die Schülerinnen und Schüler selbst die Ferienprojekte gestalten?
runde1.text: There are many schools who assign projects over the summer. Assignments can range from a large packet of math to an even larger packet on earth science. These packets are generally designed by teachers, but what if students designed them instead? If students designed these projects, then they would be more interesting than a packet with a hundred problems to be answered. If students design assignments for their peers then they'll be far less boring and more likely to get done. In the classroom, students will listen to their teachers ramble on, and not truly hear a word they say. What these instructors are saying isn't really catching the student's attention, it's boring them.

runde1.aufgabe_de: Sommerprojekte: Sollten Lehrkräfte oder die Schülerinnen und Schüler selbst die Ferienprojekte gestalten?
runde1.text: Summer projects are one of those things that every student complains about, including me. But I understand why schools give them. Three months is a long time to go without using your brain for school stuff, and it's easy to come back in the fall feeling rusty. The real question is who should design these projects. In my opinion, summer projects should be teacher-designed, because teachers know what students need to learn, they can keep the workload reasonable, and they can make sure the projects are actually graded fairly. The biggest reason is that teachers understand the curriculum and students usually don't. When I start a class in September, I have no idea what's going to be on the syllabus.

runde1.aufgabe_de: Sommerprojekte: Sollten Lehrkräfte oder die Schülerinnen und Schüler selbst die Ferienprojekte gestalten?
runde1.text: Every summer, millions of students set aside their textbooks for nearly three months, and many schools respond by assigning summer projects to keep learning going. The real debate is about who should be in charge of designing that work. Although teachers bring expertise, I believe summer projects should be student-designed. Allowing students to create their own projects builds genuine engagement, develops the self-direction they will need as adults, and respects the fact that learning does not only happen in a classroom. To begin with, students learn best when they care about what they are studying. During the school year, the curriculum is set, and students must study topics whether they find them interesting or not.

runde1.aufgabe_de: Fernunterricht: Sollten Schülerinnen und Schüler von zu Hause aus am Unterricht teilnehmen können?
runde1.text: Imagine two high school juniors. One wakes at six, catches a bus at seven, and sits through a day of classes in a building forty minutes from home. The other wakes at seven-thirty, logs into the same classes from a desk in her bedroom, and uses the time she saved to work a part-time job in the afternoon. Both learn the same material from the same teachers. The difference is that the second student had a choice. I believe students benefit from being able to attend classes from home, because it gives them control over how they learn, makes education more accessible, and prepares them for a world in which much of life already happens online.

runde2.quelle: TOEFL-Aufsatz (Englisch als Fremdsprache), Liang et al. 2023
runde2.text: An enjoyable event that took place in my childhood was when I got my first dog--- Little. I was ten and had been pestering my parents for a dog for years. One day I came home from school, my parents said they had a surprise for me and it was waiting for me in my room. I ran up to my room and threw open the door. I found a tiny puppy with a red bow around his neck and sleeping at the foot of my bed. We became good friends forever. And for the rest of his life, he slept on the exact same spot at the end of my bed every night.

I learned the definition of cancer at the age of fourteen. I was taking my chapter 7 biology test when I came upon the last question, "What is cancer?", to which I answered: "The abnormal, unrestricted growth of cells." After handing in the test, I moved on to chapter 8, oblivious then to how earth-shattering such a disease could be. I learned the meaning of cancer two years later. A girl named Kiersten came into my family by way of my oldest brother who had fallen in love with her. I distinctly recall her hair catching the sea breeze as she walked with us along the Jersey shore, a blonde wave in my surrounding family's sea of brunette.

"You're such a hipster." It's a phrase heard everyday in school hallways across America, and its usage often operates as a conundrum that obscures teenagers' perceptions of themselves and who they want to be. I, in turn, have struggled immensely with the paradoxical use of this label. Since the onset of my tween years and perhaps even before that, I have constantly carried with me an insistent urge for nonconformity; it has never sat well with me to be like everyone else. Throughout my middle school years, this natural instinct of mine manifested itself in many different ways: jeans tucked into knee-high socks, anything from punk to Harlem renaissance jazz bellowing from my headphones, Palahniuk novels peeking out of my backpack.

druck.aufgabe_de: Fernunterricht: Sollten Schülerinnen und Schüler von zu Hause aus am Unterricht teilnehmen können?
druck.text: Technology has made it possible for students to sit in on a lesson from almost anywhere, and some schools now let students choose whether to attend in person or from home. At first glance this seems like pure progress: more choice, less commuting, and lessons available to anyone with a laptop. Yet when I think about what school actually does for young people, I am convinced that most students would not benefit from attending classes from home.

druck.text: Teacher Designed Summer Projects Summer finally comes to an end and all students have completed their student designed summer project. Students are one month into school and realize the summer projects they created has not helped them prepare for school. Students are put into a horrible scenario, where they are mentally not prepared for school and are assigned many assignments they cant keep up with. It is a teachers job to create projects, tests, and assignments to help further improve a students ability to learn and understand the subject.
